source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Electrical-Body and Chassis, p.12-11

procedures.title: Headlamp vacuum relay replacement
steps: Carefully pull the 4 hoses off the relay.
Remove the 2 relay screws and lift the relay out.
Install in reverse order and check the headlamp covers work under vacuum.
notes: Put each color-coded hose back on its own fitting; Corvette fittings have molded R-Y-G letters and the hoses are color striped.

procedures.title: Headlamp vacuum tank replacement
steps: Remove the power brake booster and master cylinder (see Section 5).
Disconnect the tank hoses, noting each hose stripe color and position, and tape the hose ends to keep dirt out.
From under the left fender skirt, remove the screw assemblies holding the tank.
From inside the engine compartment, lift out the tank with its built-in brackets.

procedures.title: Headlamp vacuum hose routing
steps: Route replacement hoses so they are not pinched.
Use the exact-length actuator-to-relay hoses for each side.

Connect: manifold vacuum to check valve; check valve to tank; check valve to headlamp switch; headlamp switch to relay valve; tank to relay valve; relay valve to the closed side and to the open side of each actuator; and (Corvette) manual control valve to relay valve.
notes: Many Corvette hoses are color striped and bundled. See figure 19 in the manual.

procedures.title: Tail, stop, directional and backup lamp bulb replacement
steps: Remove the lens screws and free the lens.
Change the bulb and check the lamp works.
